claims.text: Controlled modification of the ligand coordination environment shifts the d-band center of transition-metal sites.
The position of the d-band center directly governs catalytic activity.
The position of the d-band center directly governs catalytic selectivity.
Catalysts with d-band centers shifted relative to a baseline will exhibit reproducible differences in reaction kinetics.
Catalysts with d-band centers shifted relative to a baseline will exhibit reproducible differences in product distribution.
Changing the precursor or treatment atmosphere can modify ligand coordination at metal sites.
Precursor or atmosphere-induced ligand modifications can shift the metal d-band center.
The metal d-band-center position can be probed using XPS or UPS.
Alterations in ligand coordination change the electronic structure of transition-metal sites.
A shift in the d-band center modulates the adsorption energies of reactants on the catalyst surface.
A shift in the d-band center modulates the adsorption energies of reaction intermediates on the catalyst surface.
Changes in reactant and intermediate adsorption energies affect catalytic activity.
Changes in reactant and intermediate adsorption energies affect catalytic selectivity.
A d-band-center shift of approximately 0.2 eV or more from baseline will produce a measurable change in catalytic activity.
A d-band-center shift of approximately 0.2 eV or more from baseline will alter catalytic selectivity.
The proposed relationship is limited to reactions whose mechanisms are sensitive to adsorption energies.
The proposed relationship may not apply when catalytic behavior is dominated by mass-transport limitations.
The proposed relationship may not apply when bulk properties rather than surface electronic effects control the reaction.
The magnitude and direction of the catalytic-performance change depend on the metal, reaction, and degree of coordination modification.
Support effects and catalyst morphology may independently influence the measured catalytic outcome.
